slides.say: Now a new question. Two regular hexagons have areas one hundred fifty root three and thirty root three. What is the ratio of the perimeter of the first hexagon to the perimeter of the second?
So we know the two areas, and they ask about the perimeters. We'll solve it in two different ways.
Let's start with the math way, with polygons and no similarity. Remember, a regular hexagon is made of six equilateral triangles.

slides.say: An equilateral triangle with side a has the area a squared root three over four. So the hexagon is six times that.
at: An equilateral triangle with side a

slides.say: For the first hexagon, six times a squared root three over four is equal to one hundred fifty root three.
Root three is on both sides, so it cancels. And one hundred fifty divided by six is twenty-five. So a squared over four is twenty-five.
at: one hundred fifty divided by six

slides.say: We multiply by four, so a squared is one hundred. So a is ten.
For the second hexagon, let's call its side b. In the same way, thirty divided by six is five. So b squared over four is five.
So b squared is twenty, and b is root twenty. Twenty is four times five, so root twenty is two root five.
Now the perimeters. A hexagon has six sides. So the first perimeter is six times ten, and the second is six times two root five.
The sixes cancel, so it's ten to two root five. We divide both by two, and it's five to root five.
And five is root five times root five. So we divide both by root five, and it's root five to one.

slides.say: Now with similarity. Two regular hexagons are similar, because they're regular shapes of the same kind.
The areas give us the area ratio. One hundred fifty root three is five times thirty root three. So the area ratio is five to one.

slides.say: From lengths to areas we square. So from areas back to lengths, we take the square root. Root five to root one, which is root five to one.
A perimeter is a line, so the perimeters keep that linear ratio, root five to one. All we did was go back from the area ratio to the linear ratio.
